Shoplogix Smart Factory

## Real time visiblity into your shopfloor, with tools for continuous improvement every shift

## Complete visibility of what’s happening every shift, at all times

A single manufacturing plant can lose millions of dollars every year on unplanned downtimes, waste,
and hidden shopfloor issues without a proper system in place
* **Empower your operators with intuitive visuals** of OEE, expected vs. actual targets, cycle
  speeds, scrap, unplanned downtimes, and much more
* **Purpose-built issue tracking** for your frontline teams to identify problems without
  interrupting their work
* **Hit more targets** with real-time monitoring and summary reports for your daily meetings

[ Learn more ][53]

## Eliminate more constraints with fully connected production teams

Because you aren’t replacing batteries or sending analysts out for routine inspections.

**Resolve issues faster** with your own plant-wide alerting system

[Learn more →][54]

**Build a culture of continuous improvement** with kanban tools to track improvements

[Learn more →][55]

**Improved quality checks and maintenance service times** with a Quality (QMS) and maintenance
(CMMS) system linked to your shifts and machine usage.

[Learn more →][56]

## Skip the data headaches with built in business intelligence (BI) and AI insights

**No data exporting needed:** we have an API if you need it, but our world class analytics portal
empowers you to start slicing and dicing your data on day one

[Learn more →][57]

**Compare and trend all your production data**, from any shift, machine, job order, or geographic
location

[Learn more →][58]

**No shift calendar confusion:** unlike third-party analytics tools that only understand the 24-hour
clock, ours reads from your shift calendars, so you always get accurate results

[Learn more →][59]

## **Since the implementation of Shoplogix, we were able to start addressing our main priorities**

Anibal Andreano,
Area Leader, MAGNA

## Don’t fall behind in the digital transformation journey

Smart manufacturers who need to keep up in a rapidly changing world economy need solutions that
supercharge their existing workflows (and not work against them). With Shoplogix, you get:

**Real time visibility of your shopfloor at all times: **

Empowered operators who can see their progress and act in real-time

**Powerful tools to uncover and eliminate bottlenecks hiding in plain sight: **

You’ll always know the biggest constraints holding you back (by shift, machine, job order)

**World class business intelligence (BI), connected to your production data 24/7:** No need to
manually export your data into Power BI or Tableau. You get your own BI platform out of the box,
built on top of your shift calendar and production data. And yes, we’re actively building AI
features that bring real value to our customers!

**A fully connected workforce to close all workflow gaps and win back capacity: **

Purpose-built tools for your Operators, CI Managers, Quality team, and Maintenance team, all sharing
the same data and triggering workflow actions

**A plant wide alerting system with status updates for your teams: **

Magnetic or bolt-on attachment, no downtime during setup.

self-serve demos

#### Optimization Tutorial

Solvers, or optimizers, are software tools that help users determine the best way to allocate scarce
resources. Examples include allocating money to investments, or locating new warehouse facilities,
or scheduling hospital operating rooms. In each case, multiple decisions need to be made in the best
possible way while simultaneously satisfying a number of requirements (or constraints). The "best"
or optimal solution might mean maximizing profits, minimizing costs, or achieving the best possible
quality. Here are some representative examples of optimization problems:
* Finance/Investment: Cash management, capital budgeting, portfolio optimization.
* Manufacturing: Job shop scheduling, blending, cutting stock problems.
* Distribution and Networks: Routing, truck loading, fleet scheduling.

#### Simulation/Risk Analysis Tutorial

Quantitative risk analysis is the practice of creating a mathematical model of a project or process
that explicitly includes uncertain parameters that we cannot control, and also decision variables
that we can control. Monte Carlo simulation explores thousands of possible scenarios, and calculates
the impact of the uncertain parameters and the decisions we make on outcomes that we care about --
such as profit and loss, investment returns, environmental results and more. Industries where
simulation and risk analysis are heavily used include:
* Pharmaceuticals: Modeling R&D and clinical trials
* Oil & Gas: Modeling drilling projects
* Insurance: Modeling frequency and types of claims

#### Data Science Tutorial

Data science software tools help users find patterns and hidden relationships in data, that can be
used to predict behavior and make better business decisions. A machine learning algorithm "trained"
on past observations can be used to predict the likelihood of future outcomes such as customer
"churn'" or classify new transactions into categories such as "legitimate" or "suspicious". Other
methods can be used uncover "clusters" of similar observations, or find associations among different
items. Common applications include:
* Financial Services: Fraud detection, good vs. bad credit risks
* Direct Marketing: Segmentation to improve response rates
* Electoral Politics: Identifying "most persuadable" voters
